aBigEditor.text: Option A: bigger card editor (mockup, not picked)

aBigSticky.text:
Option A · Bigger card editor
A wide sheet instead of the side panel: pictures get most of the room, and text cards get big front and back fields. Drag boxes, type, and switch types to try it. Not picked: the app uses Option B.

aCardsScreen.text: Option B: whole screen, cards on the left (picked, now in the app)

aCardsSticky.text:
Option B · Whole screen, cards on the left (in the app now)
A screen of its own, opened from the deck: its cards down the left, the one you pick in a big editor on the right. Changes save as you type (a card missing its answer waits, and says so); a new card waits at the top until Add card (⌘↵), which starts the next one. On a computer the app opens it for New card and for any card you click; phones keep the iPhone editor. Click cards, New card, types, and boxes to try it.

aMore.text: Settings, list view, icon options, and card editor types

aSticky.text:
A · Sidebar
Everything is one click away. Best for big decks and for managing lots of cards. Like Linear or Notion.

bSticky.text:
B · Top tabs
One centered column with lots of white space. Calm and simple, but less room for side panels.

bTitle.text: B · Top tabs: one calm column

cSticky.text:
C · Focus
The app opens on your next card. Decks, stats, and AI sit behind small icons. The most minimal, but managing cards takes an extra tap.
